speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain; to help me understand the severity and cause, can you please tell me when these symptoms started and if they are constant or intermittent?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave syndrome (esophageal rupture). The combination of forceful vomiting following heavy alcohol consumption, subsequent retching/choking, and the development of chest pain in a 51-year-old male is highly suggestive of esophageal perforation. Given the severity, please proceed immediately with a Water-Soluble Chest X-Ray (Gastrografin swallow) and a CT scan of the chest with oral contrast to confirm the diagnosis.
